final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; they mainly narrowed and caveated their position using the same record. That reinterpretation is substantively more careful, but it does not cure the missing compliance predicate. Under the policy, a weakness is material if it affects a named launch use case or named customer commitment. The existing evidence shows the Spanish-language billing support segment misses target by 2.1 percentage points, is named in three international pilot commitments, and remains under unresolved legal review as to disclosure. The release policy requires such a material limitation to be resolved, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. No admissible evidence establishes any of those conditions. Public governance guidance about documenting limitations and monitoring risk can support good governance posture, but it is complementary only and cannot substitute for the internal policy requirement. The Actor's narrowed framing might support a carefully caveated narrative in an audit packet, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the caveat here is itself an unresolved compliance condition, not merely residual risk.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still shows a 2.1 percentage point miss in Spanish-language billing support for a segment named in three international pilot commitments, which is material under the stated policy.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure was completed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering this specific material limitation before launch.
Legal review remains open, so the policy predicate is unresolved at certification time.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate disclosure-or-risk-acceptance requirement.
